correctness.rationale: Surjectivity and monotonicity fix the images of the bottom and top. Above a maximal bottom-fiber element s, take a saturated chain to a back-lift of each middle point. The first strict successor has that middle label: it is no longer bottom, and monotonicity bounds it by the lifted label. Thus n−|s|≥m. At n=m the bottom fiber contains only the empty set, all singleton labels are distinct middle labels, and rank ≥2 is forced to top. Coordinate deletion is an onto bounded morphism, so precomposition gives existence for all larger n. At n=m+1 the bottom fiber can additionally contain only singleton worlds. With no zero singleton, all middle labels occur already at rank one; there is either one top singleton or one duplicated label. Only the pair of duplicate-label singletons allows a further choice, producing m!(m+1)². With a nonempty zero set S, each zero singleton sees all m middle labels exactly once among its immediate successors. This forces distinct middle labels on the outside singletons and colors the pairs in S by the z−1 remaining specified labels, one of each at every vertex. Each color is therefore a perfect matching, so z=1 or z is even, and for even z such a decomposition is available by the standard round-robin construction. For any triple there are two different middle labels below it: either on two distinct outside singletons, on an outside singleton and a pair in S, or on two incident pairs in S. Thus all ranks ≥3 are top. The constructions exhaust monotonicity and the upward back requirements: each bottom point sees all labels and any middle point sees the full-set top. Counting chosen S, injective outside labels and proper colorings verifies the stated formula with fixed labels and handles z=1 separately. Independent monotone-map enumeration and a separate perfect-matching enumeration agreed with the supported finite checks; the all-m result comes from the bijection, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: Direct replay of the first-excess maps covers m=2,3, with counts 30 and 162. The counts 1080 and 9360 for m=4,5 are formula evaluations using independently counted F₂=1, F₄=6, and F₆=720, not full direct enumeration of those maps.

originality.rationale: The indexed rectangular-grid-to-diamond count covers N(2,2)=2 exactly, and the branching-threshold record treats the identical target on rooted trees. The former does not give B_3→Q_2 and neither gives the first-excess Boolean family. Standard one-factorization definitions and their small counts receive full prior credit. The supported distinction is the general Boolean first-excess classification, which identifies precisely which labelled frame-map choices correspond to labelled complete-graph factorizations, including the exceptional z=0 and z=1 strata. This is not an originality claim for the same-day diamond boundary instance, a priority ordering among same-day records, or the graph counts themselves.
residual_risks: The original mentions earlier Boolean chain or diamond work without identifying all the exact sources. A specialized enumeration might overlap more than the identified N(2,2) case.
The same-day records' priority is unresolved; their actual overlap and limits are credited regardless.

checked_sources: Kaski et al., factorization definition and switching context
value.rationale: The first excess after the sharp existence threshold is the first place an internal choice of zero singletons changes the structure of the quotient. A compatibility condition between their shared successors is shown to encode full one-factorizations of complete graphs, not merely a similar sequence of small integers. This bijection explains the excluded odd strata and expresses a natural labelled quotient census using a well-established graph invariant. The significance is the structural transfer and exact boundary classification, not computing a known graph count anew.
residual_risks: No enumeration for general n>m+1 and no faster algorithm for large F_z are claimed.
